lyrics:
[intro]
[verse]
The coffee's cold inside the ceramic mug
I trace the patterns in the dusty floor
There's no one here to offer up a hug
I stop and listen by the heavy door
[chorus]
And the silence has a heavy sort of weight
It fills the corners where we used to stand
I'm learning how to sit and accept my fate
With nothing but this shadow in my hand
[verse]
The sunlight fades behind the velvet drape
It leaves the room in shades of muted blue
I'm looking for a way to make escape
From every single dream I had of you
[chorus]
And the silence has a heavy sort of weight
It fills the corners where we used to stand
I'm learning how to sit and accept my fate
With nothing but this shadow in my hand
[bridge]
Maybe time will soften up the edges
Of these walls that keep me held so tight
I'm standing on the very sharpest ledges
Waiting for the dawn to break the night
[chorus]
And the silence has a heavy sort of weight
It fills the corners where we used to stand
I'm learning how to sit and accept my fate
With nothing but this shadow in my hand
[outro]
